Independent derivation using the pairwise-difference variance and discrete/continuous centered moments
correctness.rationale: Composing the scalar step gives weights w_j=(1−q)q^(n−j) and deterministic multiplier q^n. At uniform permutation the exact centered-noise variance is s²/(n−1) times the sum of (v_i−v_j)² over i<j; this follows from fixed total and exchangeable coordinates. Pairing replaces v by (w+w∘σ⁻¹)/2, preserving its total. Minimizing this pairwise-difference sum is equivalent to minimizing the cross dot product. Swapping any ascending pair in w∘σ⁻¹ strictly lowers the dot product, so the unique minimum is the reverse order. Because w_j w_(n+1−j)=(1−q)²q^(n−1), exact geometric sums give the two stated variances. The reversed covariance is strictly negative by AM–GM on the nonconstant weights; reverse averages are constant for n=2 only, since the first and second averages differ by (1−q)²(1−q^(n−2))/2. Fresh independent epochs give the exact geometric second-moment sum and unchanged stationary ratio. Independently checked the small-step coefficient by centering the linear and reversal-even quadratic terms in the geometric weights: their leading squared norms give (1−q)² Var((t−mean(t))²)/(4 Var(t))=(1−q)²(n²−4)/60 for uniform t on 0,…,n−1. For q=1−λ/n the centered position profiles after multiplying by n converge to λe^(−λt) and its reversal average; their variances yield U and B. The increasing/decreasing exponential profiles have strictly negative covariance under uniform t, hence 0<B<U/2. The continuum centered moments 1/12 and 1/180 give B/U∼λ²/60; the large-λ terms and the fixed-q geometric sums both give 1/2 in their respective regimes.
residual_risks: Uniqueness is only for fixed position rearrangements, q strictly between 0 and 1, and nonconstant centers. Stationarity requires fresh independent permutation pairs. Two same-input passes, not two consecutive updates, are being averaged.

value.rationale: The precise comparison is useful as an exact variance benchmark for a previously proposed way to spend two full passes: two independent same-input passes would give half the ordinary innovation variance, whereas the reverse pair is strictly below that baseline, optimizes the specified class, and has a quantified low-epoch-step advantage and a saturation regime. The full crossover and constants are the useful model result, not merely the classical rearrangement or the affine stationarity formula.
residual_risks: Not a wall-clock or objective-convergence improvement for arbitrary losses, nor a comparison with two sequential training epochs.
